meta.name: 22 Kalliope
meta.note: 22 Kalliope (M-type) is a main-belt asteroid; this is its brightness in 152 SPHEREx frames, each frame at a different wavelength, not a reflectance spectrum.
meta.method: The position of the asteroid at each SPHEREx exposure comes from JPL Horizons as seen from the SPHEREx spacecraft, and every exposure whose detector held that position was cut out. The flux is the sum of the calibrated image inside a 3-pixel-radius circle at the centroid, minus the median of a sky ring, times the pixel size, and the wavelength is read at that pixel.
caveats: These are fluxes, not reflectance: the Sun's spectrum is not divided out and no thermal model is fitted. Thermal emission from the asteroid itself dominates beyond about 3.5 um for asteroids this close to the Sun.
Each frame sees the asteroid at a different time and at a different wavelength, so rotation (brightness changes with spin) and wavelength are mixed between neighbouring points.
Centroids are good to about 1 arcsec from 6.15 arcsec pixels; this is not MPC-grade astrometry. Positions are as seen from the SPHEREx spacecraft; Horizons times are matched to the exposure mid-time.

Pixels the SPHEREx pipeline flagged OUTLIER are kept because a moving object is flagged that way; frames with a saturated pixel in the aperture (26), with a masked or non-finite pixel in the aperture (30), with another source within 6 pixels (6), too near the detector edge (0), centred on a source more than 6 arcsec from the prediction (0) or without usable sky (0) were removed, out of 220 frames examined; points with S/N below 5 are kept and have no measured centroid.
No aperture correction and no colour correction; the aperture holds about 98% of a point source.
